walkthroughs.body_html:
An ecosystem has living and non-living parts.

Biotic: plants and animals. Abiotic: rocks, water, climate.

All are linked in delicate balance.

Energy flows through trophic levels.

Producers capture sunlight; consumers eat them.

Decomposers return nutrients to the soil.

walkthroughs.body_html:
At larger scale, ecosystems group into biomes.

Climate (rain and temperature) decides which biome forms.

Examples: rainforest, tundra, desert.

mcqs.q: Why are tropical rainforest soils typically infertile?
options: Heavy rainfall leaches nutrients, and most nutrients are stored in living biomass and rapidly recycled — the soil itself holds very little.
Large scale means the map is physically big.
Because so much vegetation grows there, the soil must be fertile.
Because rainforest soils are made of clay.

options: Biotic means animals and abiotic means plants.

mcqs.q: What does a 'large scale' map mean?
options: A large-scale map covers a small area in high detail (e.g. 1:25,000 OS map of one town); a small-scale map covers a large area in less detail (e.g. 1:1,000,000 world atlas).
